channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Nigeria retains Africa’s top oil producer status despite missing OPEC quota
item.description: Nigeria has retained its position as Africa’s largest crude oil producer after raising output to 1.45 million barrels per day in March, according to the latest monthly report from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

item.title: Congo says it’s ready to look elsewhere if U.S. minerals framework fails
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo could pursue other international partners if its minerals cooperation framework with the United States does not result in concrete investment projects.

item.title: Indonesia, Ecuador and Nigeria on standby to replace Ghana as world’s second-largest cocoa producer
item.description: Ghana’s prolonged production slump and financial strain in its cocoa sector are increasingly raising the prospect that the West African nation could lose its long-held position as the world’s second-largest cocoa producer.

item.title: Dangote refinery hits full capacity: What it means for the naira
item.description: Nigeria’s foreign exchange market may be entering a more hopeful phase following confirmation that the Dangote Petroleum Refinery has reached full operational capacity. The refinery, which can process 650,000 barrels of crude a day, is the largest single-train facility of its kind in the world.

item.title: Nigeria’s oil giant records $4.2 billion in profit as output nears 1.6 million barrels daily
item.description: Nigeria’s state-owned oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC), has reported an after-tax profit of $4.26 billion for 2025, underlining strong revenue performance despite production fluctuations and maintenance outages.

item.title: Australia-backed uranium mine in Namibia is set to have a great year as nuclear demand surges
item.description: The Langer Heinrich uranium mine in Namibia, which primarily supplies resources for nuclear power plants, is nearing its full operational capacity.

item.title: From airstrikes to investigations, the U.S. aims to escalate pressure on the Nigerian government
item.description: From launching airstrikes aimed at terrorist groups in Nigeria to deploying a tactical team, the United States now intends to get an “assessment of Nigeria’s compliance with the International Religious Freedom.

item.title: BAT says it warned South Africa about illicit tobacco for years
item.description: British American Tobacco Plc had repeatedly warned the South African government that it might halt local production by the end of 2026 if authorities failed to curb the surge in illicit cigarette sales, according to its chief executive.

item.title: Despite travel warnings from Canada, U.S. and China, South Africa records historic 10.5 million visitors in 2025
item.description: South Africa’s tourism sector reached a historic milestone in 2025, welcoming a record 10.5 million international visitors despite travel warnings issued by Canada, the U.S., China and Australia, surpassing pre-pandemic figures and signalling renewed global confidence in the country as a premier travel destination.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the lowest fuel prices in February 2026
item.description: With global oil markets shifting and domestic currencies increasingly influencing pricing results, low fuel costs are delivering much-needed respite to individuals, businesses, and governments alike. For many African countries, prolonged reductions in fuel costs provide numerous advantages.
